final_answer: Deliver the autonomous idea-approval capability by EXTENDING the existing intake path, not as a new gate or daemon. Add-Idea keeps calling the fast, deterministic, fail-closed Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate (lib/backlog.ps1) first for dedup / evidence / hard-policy checks; ideas that survive are judged inside the existing Invoke-BacklogCurator (lib/backlog-core.ps1). The curator wraps its existing LLM judge (Claude on the prepaid plan, per the goals.md economy priority) with a deterministic, fail-closed risk classifier in lib/policy.ps1: any idea touching the control plane (driver/supervisor/watchdog/secrets/circuit-breaker), security, irreversible operations, or architectural pivots is forced to operator-required regardless of the LLM verdict. The LLM scores each surviving idea against goals.md on relevance, utility, and effectiveness — each score citing the concrete goal line it advances, so the rubric is auditable rather than a vibe check. The curator then applies asymmetric thresholds (tau_approve >> tau_reject): auto-approve is the narrow path requiring low-risk + clear scope + demonstrable goal benefit + clear causal path + high confidence + a pass from the deterministic classifier; clearly-identified junk/duplicates/already-done/out-of-scope is auto-rejected; and everything uncertain, low-confidence, erroring, or merely lacking an obvious goal link under low confidence routes to operator-required — never silently dropped. The three internal verbs (approve/reject/operator-required) map onto the three existing statuses (approved/auto-dropped/held) with no new status types, keeping downstream tooling and dashboards intact. Every decision writes a structured, goal-linked rationale (verdict, confidence, linked goals, rubric scores, risk tier + reason, model, judged_at_sha, timestamp, human-readable reason) to the existing curator/judge jsonl logs. Before any live auto-approve is switched on, the whole pipeline runs in shadow/dry-run against historical operator decisions to measure precision and recall. Net effect: the idea flow is consolidated and simplified, not forked into a competing gate.

decisions.decision: Implement autonomous approval as an extension of Invoke-BacklogCurator + Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate inside the existing Add-Idea flow — no new daemon, service, or parallel gate. (atom_1)
decisions.rationale: Minimizes new surface area, reuses proven plumbing, and directly satisfies the consolidation constraint and the goals.md lesson that conflicting gates falsely block autonomy. Triple-proposal consensus; judge total 0.845.
alternatives_considered: A standalone autonomous-approval daemon polling the backlog
A new dedicated approval gate parallel to the intake gate
decisions.risk: Curator's responsibility grows; mitigated by keeping the deterministic gate and risk classifier as separate, independently testable layers.
decisions.test: No new daemon/gate process exists; the approval logic lives inside Invoke-BacklogCurator / Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate within the existing Add-Idea path.

decisions.decision: Add a deterministic, fail-closed risk classifier in lib/policy.ps1 that flags control-plane, security, irreversible, and architectural-pivot ideas and forces operator-required, overriding any LLM auto-approval. (atom_2)
decisions.rationale: This is the central safety control: it makes the catastrophic failure mode (LLM auto-approving a control-plane/security/irreversible change) structurally impossible. Cheap, high-leverage, named categories give a precise test. Highest-scoring atom (0.8875).
alternatives_considered: Trusting the LLM's own self-assessed risk
A soft LLM-advisory risk hint with no hard override
decisions.risk: Deny-list may over-block (false operator-required); acceptable under fail-closed posture and tunable from shadow-run data.
decisions.test: A deterministic classifier runs before/around the LLM, detects the four high-risk categories, and forces operator-required regardless of the LLM verdict.

decisions.decision: Score each idea with a goals.md-anchored rubric on relevance, utility, and effectiveness — MODIFIED so each dimension has an explicit operational definition and each score must cite the specific goal line it is measured against. (atom_3, judge: modify)
decisions.rationale: A goals-anchored rubric is correct, but the three dimensions overlap and are under-operationalized; without crisp, citable definitions the LLM can hand-wave scores. Operationalizing makes it auditable. Judge total 0.7775 with a 0.05 penalty for fuzziness, resolved by this modification.
alternatives_considered: Three free-form qualitative scores with no goal citation
A single blended goal-fit score
decisions.risk: Rubric still partly subjective; mitigated by requiring goal-line citations and logging scores for shadow audit.
decisions.test: LLM output includes relevance/utility/effectiveness scores, each with an operational definition and an explicit citation to the goals.md goal it is measured against.

decisions.decision: Feed the curator LLM a compact, lazily-assembled context bundle: goals.md, a compact bridge profile, current status, recent commits, similar/open/done/rejected ideas, and the policy.ps1 risk verdict. (atom_4)
decisions.rationale: Gives the judge what it needs for grounded, dedup-aware decisions; the enumerated list is precisely testable. Judge total 0.7575, dinged on simplicity/feasibility for assembly cost and token bloat — hence the compact, lazy-assembly requirement.
alternatives_considered: Judging on the idea text alone
Always loading full history regardless of relevance
decisions.risk: Token bloat / latency and assembly cost; mitigated by compact summaries and lazy loading of similar/done/rejected ideas.
decisions.test: The curator prompt demonstrably includes goals.md, bridge profile, status, commits, similar ideas, and the policy.ps1 risk verdict.

decisions.decision: Use a unified internal vocabulary (approve / reject / operator-required) mapped onto existing statuses approved / auto-dropped / held — no new status types. (atom_5)
decisions.rationale: Low-cost, high-clarity standardization that keeps downstream tooling, claim pickers, and dashboards intact. Confirmed against lib/backlog-crud.ps1 which already handles approved/auto-dropped/held. Judge total 0.8425.
alternatives_considered: Introducing new auto-approved / auto-held statuses
Reusing 'approved' for both auto and manual with no distinguishing field
decisions.risk: Loss of provenance (auto vs operator) inside a shared status; mitigated by the structured rationale fields (model, judged_at_sha) in atom_9.
decisions.test: System uses approve/reject/operator-required internally and maps them to approved/auto-dropped/held with no new statuses introduced.

decisions.decision: Gate auto-approve on a conjunction: low-risk AND clear scope AND demonstrable goal benefit AND clear causal path AND high confidence AND passing the deterministic classifier. (atom_6)
decisions.rationale: Correctly conservative — makes auto-approve the narrow, well-justified path that an autonomous approver needs. The multiple AND-conditions cost some simplicity but that strictness is the point. Judge total 0.8475.
alternatives_considered: Auto-approving on a single high goal-fit score
Approving anything not explicitly flagged risky
decisions.risk: May route many borderline-good ideas to operator-required (lower auto-approve recall); acceptable and preferable to false approvals.
decisions.test: Auto-approval logic verifies low-risk, clear scope, goal benefit, clear path, high confidence, and a pass from the deterministic safety classifier before approving.

decisions.decision: Auto-reject only clearly-identified junk, duplicates, dead/out-of-scope, already-done, and gate-clutter ideas — MODIFIED so absence of a goal link under LOW confidence routes to operator-required (per atom_8), not auto-drop. (atom_7, judge: modify)
decisions.rationale: Auto-rejecting unambiguous waste is safe and valuable, but auto-dropping ideas merely 'lacking a clear goal link' risks silently discarding good-but-poorly-phrased ideas. Deferring weak-signal cases to the operator protects recall. Judge total 0.785 with a 0.05 recall penalty resolved by this modification.
alternatives_considered: Auto-rejecting any idea without an explicit goals.md link
Never auto-rejecting and sending all rejects to the operator
decisions.risk: Some junk reaches the operator queue; acceptable trade for not losing salvageable ideas.
decisions.test: Auto-rejection fires only on clearly-identified junk/duplicates/out-of-scope/done; low-confidence no-goal-link cases land in held (operator-required), not auto-dropped.

decisions.decision: Apply asymmetric thresholds (tau_approve > tau_reject) and route all uncertainty, low-confidence approvals, and model errors to operator-required — ban silent drops. (atom_8)
decisions.rationale: Makes false-approve far harder than false-reject and forbids silent loss of ideas — the correct risk posture for an autonomous approver and a strong safety multiplier. Judge total 0.8475.
alternatives_considered: Symmetric thresholds
Defaulting errors/ambiguity to auto-reject for queue cleanliness
decisions.risk: Operator queue may grow under model uncertainty; surfaced and tunable via shadow metrics.
decisions.test: tau_approve > tau_reject is enforced; low-confidence approvals and any model error/ambiguity result in held (operator-required), never auto-drop or auto-approve.

decisions.decision: Record a structured rationale for every decision (verdict, confidence, linked goals, rubric scores, risk tier, risk reason, model, judged_at_sha, timestamp, human-readable reason) by extending the existing auto_curator / judge jsonl logs. (atom_9)
decisions.rationale: Gives full auditability, enables shadow evaluation and post-hoc rollback, and is cheap because it reuses current logging. Fully enumerated fields are directly testable and satisfy the transparency constraint. Judge total 0.8425.
alternatives_considered: Logging only the final status
A free-text reason with no structured fields
decisions.risk: Log growth and PII/secret leakage in reasons; mitigated by structured fields and the secrets constraint from goals.md.
decisions.test: auto_curator / curator-decisions.jsonl entries contain every listed field, including a goal-linked human-readable reason visible in chat/logs.

decisions.decision: Preserve Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate as the fast, deterministic, fail-closed pre-filter (dedup, evidence, hard policy) that runs BEFORE the LLM judge. (atom_10)
decisions.rationale: Defense-in-depth: stops bad inputs from ever reaching the probabilistic judge, keeps cost down, and complements the atom_2 classifier at essentially no added cost. Judge total 0.86.
alternatives_considered: Folding all checks into the LLM judge
Running the gate after the LLM
decisions.risk: Two safety layers could diverge; mitigated by keeping the gate's core deterministic functions unchanged and the classifier as a distinct policy.ps1 layer.
decisions.test: Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate retains its deterministic fail-closed functions and executes before the LLM judge in the flow.

decisions.decision: Validate the full decision logic in shadow/dry-run mode against historical operator decisions, measuring precision and recall, as a GATING PREREQUISITE before enabling any live auto-approve. (atom_11)
decisions.rationale: Best-practice de-risking and the natural payoff of atom_9's logging — measure before flipping on autonomy. Scored lower on feasibility/simplicity (0.785) due to cost and dependence on a labeled historical corpus, but the pre-go-live risk reduction is decisive.
alternatives_considered: Enabling live auto-approve immediately
Validating only on synthetic ideas
decisions.risk: Insufficient labeled history may weaken statistics; surfaced as an open question and mitigated by starting in pure-shadow with operator still deciding.
decisions.test: A shadow/dry-run mode runs the classifier+LLM without acting, logs verdicts, and its decisions are compared against historical operator decisions to compute precision/recall before live auto-approve is enabled.

rejected.decision: Build a new standalone autonomous-approval service / daemon / gate separate from the curator.
rejected.why: Directly violates the consolidation constraint and the goals.md lesson (priority: simplicity over accretion). More moving parts = slower, less reliable, and the historical cause of conflicting gates that falsely blocked autonomy. The capability must extend the existing curator/intake path instead.

rejected.decision: Let the LLM judge auto-approve based solely on its own confidence, with no deterministic safety override.
rejected.why: Fails the critical fail-closed safety constraint — an LLM hallucination or jailbreak could auto-approve a control-plane/security/irreversible/architectural-pivot change. The deterministic policy.ps1 classifier (atom_2) must be able to override the LLM to operator-required.

rejected.decision: Introduce new backlog status types for autonomous decisions (e.g. auto-approved, auto-held).
rejected.why: Breaks downstream tooling, claim pickers, and dashboards and re-adds complexity. The three internal verbs map cleanly onto the existing approved/auto-dropped/held statuses (atom_5); provenance is captured via structured rationale fields instead.

rejected.decision: Auto-reject any idea that lacks an explicit goals.md link.
rejected.why: Risks silently dropping good-but-poorly-phrased ideas, hurting recall. Per the atom_7 modification, low-confidence no-goal-link cases must route to operator-required (held), not auto-dropped.

rejected.decision: Enable live auto-approve immediately on rollout without shadow validation.
rejected.why: No measured precision/recall means unknown false-approve rate on a critical-risk control. Atom_11 makes shadow/dry-run against historical decisions a gating prerequisite before any live auto-approve.

open_questions: Is there a sufficient corpus of labeled historical operator decisions (approve/reject/held) to compute statistically meaningful precision/recall in shadow mode (atom_11 feasibility)?

What concrete numeric values for tau_approve and tau_reject, and what confidence definition, balance autonomy (fewer ideas stuck) against the fail-closed posture? To be calibrated from the shadow run, not guessed.

Does the 'held' status already surface clearly to the operator (e.g. via tools/operator-pulse.ps1 / web dashboard), or does the operator-required queue need a dedicated view so held ideas don't become a new silent backlog?

What is the exact, maintainable source of the deny-list categories in policy.ps1 (control-plane/security/irreversible/architectural-pivot), and how is it kept in sync with the goals.md hard constraints (watchdog.ps1, supervisor.ps1, .git, secrets.json, scheduler tasks)?
What token/context budget cap applies to the compact context bundle (atom_4) so curator latency and cost stay within the speed and economy priorities?

implementation_plan.detail: Submit this design record for operator approval. No code changes until sign-off (task is design-only).

Add the fail-closed risk classifier to lib/policy.ps1 (deny-list: control-plane/security/irreversible/architectural-pivot, sourced from goals.md hard constraints). Confirm Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate (lib/backlog.ps1) keeps its deterministic pre-filter unchanged and runs first. Unit-test that any high-risk category forces operator-required.

Extend the existing auto_curator / judge jsonl logging with the full structured rationale schema and the approve/reject/operator-required → approved/auto-dropped/held mapping. Logging must work before any decision is acted on.

Inside Invoke-BacklogCurator (lib/backlog-core.ps1), assemble the compact context bundle, prompt the existing LLM judge for the operationalized goals.md-cited rubric scores + confidence, and implement asymmetric thresholds and the auto-approve conjunction / narrow auto-reject / route-uncertainty-to-held logic.

Run the full pipeline in dry-run: it logs verdicts but the operator still decides. Replay historical decisions, compute precision/recall, tune tau_approve/tau_reject and the deny-list. Do NOT enable live auto-approve until precision on the safety boundary meets the agreed bar.

Flip on live auto-reject and auto-approve behind a config flag, with operator-required (held) as the default sink for anything uncertain. Monitor logs and keep the flag reversible (git-rollback per goals.md safety constraint).

next_step: Submit this design for operator approval; upon sign-off, implement Phase 1 (atom_2 deterministic risk classifier in lib/policy.ps1) plus Phase 2 (atom_9 structured rationale logging), since the fail-closed classifier is the highest-value safety control and logging is the prerequisite for the atom_11 shadow validation that gates any live auto-approve.

red_team_findings.what: The deterministic deny-list classifier is specified to run on the idea's free TEXT, but lib/policy.ps1 documents (lines 4-13) that exactly this free-text control-plane matching was REMOVED because it false-flagged safe work ('a task that merely MENTIONED driver.ps1/supervisor/secret ... was classified control-plane'). The surviving correct classifier (lines 115-122) inspects EDIT TARGETS — 'explicit edit targets, none protected => NOT control-plane (whatever the text says).' A backlog idea has no edit targets yet, so the design's risk gate must either revert to the abandoned free-text matching (reintroducing the documented false-positive failure that 'ЛОЖНО блокировало автономию' per goals.md) or it cannot classify ideas at all.
red_team_findings.why: The single load-bearing safety atom is built on a detection method the codebase already proved broken and deliberately retired. It cannot be 'sourced from policy.ps1' as claimed without resurrecting the exact anti-pattern policy.ps1 exists to kill.

red_team_findings.what: The design asserts the boundary is fail-CLOSED and 'sourced from policy.ps1 so they cannot diverge,' but policy.ps1's danger scan explicitly fails OPEN: line 174 — `if (-not $danger) { ... safe = $true; risk = 'unknown'; reason = 'danger scan unavailable (fail-open)' }` — and Test-PolicyAutotaskExecutionBlocked then returns blocked=$false for safe=true. If Test-AutonomousTaskSafe is unavailable or throws, the upstream policy defaults to NOT blocked.
red_team_findings.why: Directly violates the contract's critical fail-closed safety constraint. Reusing policy.ps1 as the risk source inherits a fail-open default, so a missing/erroring classifier (or one that can't reason about a text-only idea) lets a dangerous idea pass rather than routing to operator-required.

red_team_findings.what: Approval is not backlog hygiene — 'approved' ideas are autonomously claimed and IMPLEMENTED by the driver (driver/20-context.ps1:56-61 'will claim next runnable/approved idea'; driver/81-loop-idle-claim.ps1; recent commits show 'Автозадача из бэклога'). The deny-list keys on a short idea title, which cannot reveal an implementation's blast radius. A goal-aligned, safe-sounding idea ('ускорить главный цикл' / speed up the main loop — maps to goal #4 speed) passes every auto-approve conjunct yet its implementation necessarily edits the supervisor/driver, which goals.md line 42 forbids ('НЕ трогать watchdog.ps1, supervisor.ps1').
red_team_findings.why: Auto-approve directly triggers autonomous code changes to the control plane, but the safety check runs on text that never names the control plane. This is a fail-OPEN on the central mandate — the most dangerous ideas are precisely those whose danger is in the implementation, not the title.

red_team_findings.what: The deny-list categories (control-plane, security, irreversible, architectural pivot) omit META-changes to the safety machinery itself: ideas that modify the curator, policy.ps1/deny-list, goals.md, or the approval thresholds. Bridge goals #6 (self-development) and #7 ('Оптимизация и улучшение СВОИХ сервисов') explicitly drive the bridge to generate ideas like 'improve the backlog curator' or 'relax the over-strict risk classifier.'
red_team_findings.why: The system's own north-star incentivizes ideas that target its safety boundary, and those ideas are not on the deny-list, so the curator could autonomously approve weakening of its own guardrails — an unbounded self-modification hole on a critical-risk control.

red_team_findings.what: Routing everything dangerous/uncertain/low-confidence/erroring to 'held' (operator-required) recreates the exact stall the task exists to eliminate. For a self-improving bridge, a large fraction of generated ideas touch its own code/services (control-plane-adjacent → deny-listed → held), plus all low-confidence/ambiguous cases. The design provides no throughput floor or operator SLA — open_questions even admits 'is there an SLA so they do not re-accumulate.'
red_team_findings.why: The stated goal is to stop ideas accumulating awaiting manual approval. Under realistic load a conservative conjunction + broad deny-list pushes the majority to held, reproducing the original backlog-stall problem with extra steps.

red_team_findings.what: The design contradicts the behavior of the very function it claims to merely 'extend.' The existing Invoke-BacklogCurator (lib/backlog-core.ps1:844-853) routes confidence<0.6 to 'drop' (→ auto-dropped) and any invalid/non-JSON verdict to 'drop' (line 837), i.e. it SILENTLY DROPS under uncertainty. atom_8 explicitly rejects silent drop and mandates uncertainty→held. The design narrative does not flag that honoring atom_8 requires inverting the existing low-confidence and parse-failure paths.
red_team_findings.why: An unacknowledged behavioral delta means a literal 'extension' inherits the opposite of the intended safety policy — borderline-good and ambiguous ideas get auto-dropped and lost rather than escalated, violating atom_8 and the 'never silently drop' rejected-option.

red_team_findings.what: The design and decision record never acknowledge that Invoke-BacklogCurator ALREADY implements autonomous approve/hold/drop with model confidence, goals/status/git context, status mapping (approve→approved, hold→held, drop→auto-dropped), and a logged judge jsonl line (backlog-core.ps1:793-889). Much of the 'design' re-describes shipped behavior without specifying the actual delta versus what exists.
red_team_findings.why: Failing to scope what is NEW vs existing invites duplicate/parallel implementation — the precise documented failure mode (goals.md lines 26-31; policy.ps1 lines 4-13 '6-7 DIFFERENT detectors') the whole task is meant to avoid.

red_team_findings.what: Shadow-validation's oracle is contaminated, not just sparse. The existing curator already auto-judges ideas, so 'historical operator decisions' in the backlog are largely the OLD LLM's own auto-verdicts, not human ground truth. Measuring precision/recall against them validates new-LLM-vs-old-LLM agreement.
red_team_findings.why: It yields false confidence in the boundary before go-live. The open_question flags data sparsity but not the deeper problem that the labels themselves are machine-generated, so the go-live gate (atom_11) can pass while still being miscalibrated against real operator judgment.

red_team_findings.what: Auto-approve hinges on 'high model confidence,' which the existing code and the design take from the model's self-reported probability (backlog-core.ps1 reads obj.confidence; open_question admits the computation is undefined). LLM self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated and trivially inflatable by adversarial or self-generated idea text (the bridge authors its own ideas; an idea body could assert low risk / high benefit to nudge the judge).
red_team_findings.why: The auto-approve gate's strength rests on an unreliable, manipulable signal with no defined calibration, undermining the conjunction that is supposed to make auto-approval the safe exception.

red_team_findings.what: Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate is defined twice in the loaded libs (lib/backlog.ps1:266 and lib/backlog-workpack.ps1:585). The design treats it as the single deterministic 'front door,' but which definition wins depends on dot-source order and they can silently diverge.
red_team_findings.why: Undercuts the consolidation/'single decision point' thesis and the 'gate remains unchanged in its core fail-closed functions' test (atom_2): there isn't one canonical gate, so the fail-closed front door is ambiguous and a maintenance hazard.
